title: RAG Guardrails
tagline: The model will answer anyway. Decide what it may say, what it may read and what it may do.
story: The right chunks reached the model, and the model is about to answer. It will answer fluently whether or not the chunks support it. A retrieved page may carry hidden instructions, the user may probe for harmful output, and a tool call may leave the building. This world places guards around the whole path, prices their errors and chooses between platform services, open source and custom checks.
oneLiner: Place guards on input, retrieval, tools and output, enforce grounding, and measure what each guard costs in latency and false alarms.
youWillLearn: Place guards at input, retrieval, tool and output points and decide which run in parallel
Choose a streaming mode and explain what violating text can reach the user
Separate answerability, groundedness and citation validity, and enforce each one
Read Azure AI Content Safety and Foundry guardrails by status: GA, preview and retired
Choose between platform guards, NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Llama Guard and custom checks
Handle PII at ingest, at query time and in output
Price false positives and evaluate guards before users meet them

flashcards.front: Name the places a guard can stand around a RAG call.
flashcards.back: User input, retrieved content, tool call, tool response and output. Foundry exposes input, tool call (preview), tool response (preview) and output. NeMo names input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output rails.

flashcards.front: Why do independent guards run in parallel?
flashcards.back: Parallel guards add only the slowest one's latency, while sequential guards add up. No vendor page checked on 2026-10-13 publishes guard latency, so measure each guard.

flashcards.front: What is the trade-off of Azure's asynchronous filter streaming mode?
flashcards.back: No filter latency and token-by-token streaming, but the stop signal is guaranteed only within about a 1,000-character window, so violating text can reach the user first.

flashcards.front: What does the default streaming mode do with filtering?
flashcards.back: It buffers completion text, filters each buffer and returns content chunks, not token by token. It is safer than asynchronous mode and delivers the first chunk later.

flashcards.front: How does a Foundry agent's guardrail relate to its model's guardrail?
flashcards.back: It fully overrides it. An agent guardrail with no tool-call or tool-response controls leaves those unscanned. With no custom guardrail the agent inherits the model's.

flashcards.front: What are Prompt Shields' two shields?
flashcards.back: User prompt attacks (jailbreaks) and document (indirect) attacks. The standalone API takes one `userPrompt` and up to five `documents` and returns `attackDetected`. It was tested on English only.

flashcards.front: What does Azure Spotlighting do, and what does it cost?
flashcards.back: It marks documents as lower trust by base64 encoding them (preview, off by default, Chat Completions models only). Token counts rise and the model may mention base64.

flashcards.front: What does a citation prove?
flashcards.back: Provenance, not entailment. A cited span can still contradict the claim, so add a quote-first step or a claim-level support check.

flashcards.front: Which three checks sit around grounding?
flashcards.back: Answerability before generation, groundedness after generation (is each claim entailed?) and citation validity (does each cited span exist and support the claim?).

flashcards.front: What are the Azure groundedness detection limits?
flashcards.back: Optimised for English, grounding sources 55,000 characters, text plus query 7,500, query at least 3 words. Reasoning mode explains ungrounded segments and suits development.

flashcards.front: Name NeMo Guardrails' five rail types.
flashcards.back: Input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output. Retrieval rails filter chunks and execution rails check tool calls.

flashcards.front: What happens to NeMo's `self check facts` rail with a reasoning model?
flashcards.back: If the model spends its `max_tokens` budget thinking, the rail fails closed: score 0.0 and the response is blocked. Raise the budget or use a non-reasoning checker.

flashcards.front: Why does Llama Guard suit a custom policy?
flashcards.back: It is a classifier whose category text you can rewrite in the prompt, so a custom taxonomy needs no retraining. Llama Guard 4 is 12B, multimodal and runs on one GPU.

flashcards.front: What does the Presidio documentation warn about?
flashcards.back: That it cannot guarantee it finds all PII. Test on your own formats, add custom recognizers and layer other controls.

flashcards.front: What is the scope of the Foundry PII filter?
flashcards.back: Model output only (preview). Entity types follow Azure Language categories, and the action is annotate or annotate and block, which blocks the whole output.

flashcards.front: Why is guard precision low even with a good classifier?
flashcards.back: Base rates. At 0.5% harmful traffic, 95% recall and a 2% false positive rate, only about 19% of blocks are real harm.

flashcards.front: Why start a guard in shadow mode (annotate only)?
flashcards.back: It measures real block rates and false positives on live traffic before any user is blocked, and shows which categories and languages need tuning.

flashcards.front: What is the status of Custom categories (standard) on 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Its retirement date, 2026-09-01, has passed. The concept page still says retiring and points to Foundry custom text classification. Confirm in the portal. Rapid is preview.

flashcards.front: What should a guard do on a timeout in a regulated assistant?
flashcards.back: Fail closed or degrade to abstain or escalate. Treating a timeout as a pass is a fail-open bug, and the guard timeout rate needs an alert.

flashcards.front: What are the protected material limits worth remembering?
flashcards.back: Text and code detection are English only, the code index is current only through 2023-04-06, and completions need at least 110 characters to be scanned.

glossary.def: A named set of controls. Each control pairs a risk, an intervention point, a severity threshold and an action.
A place where a guardrail scans content: user input, tool call, tool response or output. Tool call and tool response are agent-only previews.
Azure AI Content Safety detectors for user prompt attacks (jailbreaks) and document (indirect) attacks.
Instructions hidden in a document, web page, email or tool result that the model reads as if the user had written them.
Marking untrusted text so the model can tell it from instructions. Azure's version base64 encodes documents and is a preview feature.
The share of an answer's claims that the supplied sources support. It is a property of each claim, not of the whole answer.
Whether the retrieved evidence contains an answer at all. It is checked before generation.
A claim is entailed when the source text implies it. NLI models score this and back many groundedness checks.
Known copyrighted text or licensed code that a completion reproduces. Azure detects text and code matches.
NeMo Guardrails' name for a guard: input, retrieval, dialog, execution or output.
When a guard cannot decide, the request is refused or sent to review. The opposite, fail open, lets it through.
A benign request or answer that a guard blocks. Its cost is lost help and user trust.
Annotate records a verdict and lets the content through. Block stops it. Annotate is how you run a guard in shadow mode.
Meta's open safety classifier models. The prompt lists hazard categories, and you can rewrite that text for a custom taxonomy.
An open-source toolkit that detects and anonymizes PII with recognizers that combine NER, regex, rules and context.

claims.text: Foundry guardrails support four intervention points: user input, tool call (preview, agents only), tool response (preview, agents only) and output.
Foundry guardrail actions are annotate and annotate and block, and agents support annotate and block only (preview).

An agent's guardrail fully overrides its model deployment's guardrail, and the guardrail system applies only to agents developed in Foundry Agent Service, not to other agents registered in the Foundry Control Plane.

In default streaming, completion text is buffered, filtered and returned in chunks. In asynchronous filter mode the filtering signal is guaranteed only within a roughly 1,000-character window, and configuring it requires permission to modify content filtering policies.
NeMo Guardrails has five rail types: input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output. Retrieval rails filter chunks and execution rails check tool calls.

Azure groundedness detection offers domain (Medical, Generic) and task (Summarization, QnA) options, a non-reasoning fast mode and a reasoning mode that explains ungrounded segments, optional correction (preview), and accuracy optimised for English.
The groundedness detection API (preview) limits are 55,000 characters of grounding sources per call, 7,500 characters of text plus query, and a minimum query length of 3 words.

NeMo's self check facts output rail uses $relevant_chunks as evidence and returns a score from 0.0 to 1.0, and it fails closed (score 0.0, response blocked) if a reasoning model spends its max_tokens budget before answering.
Anthropic guidance recommends explicit permission to say I don't know and, for documents over 20k tokens, asking for word-for-word quotes first.
Enabling Anthropic citations together with structured outputs returns HTTP 400.
SummaC applies sentence-level NLI and aggregates the results to detect inconsistency.

The Foundry guardrail controls table lists Spotlighting, Groundedness, Personally identifiable information and Task Adherence as Preview, and Spotlighting and Groundedness are not yet supported for agents.

The default safety policy sets hate and fairness, violence, sexual and self-harm to Medium on prompts and completions, covers user prompt injection attacks on prompts, and covers protected material text and code on completions.

Prompt Shields has user prompt attack and document attack shields. The standalone API takes one userPrompt and up to five documents and returns attackDetected. It has been GA since August 2024 and was tested on English only.
Azure Spotlighting is off by default, works with the Chat Completions API and models only, tags documents by base64 encoding them, and raises token counts.
The Spotlighting paper reports attack success falling from above 50% to below 2% on GPT-family models with minimal task impact.
Protected material detection is English only, the code scanner index is current only through 2023-04-06, and completions are scanned from a default minimum of 110 characters.
Custom categories (standard) was scheduled to retire on 2026-09-01 and the page points to Foundry Custom text classification, while Custom categories (rapid) uses an LLM for emerging incidents.

Content Safety input limits: analyze text 10K characters, Prompt Shields prompt 10K characters with up to five documents totalling 10K, protected material minimum 110 characters, and Foundry guardrails moderate the first 1,000 characters for text scenarios (scope unclear).
Foundry guardrails use four severity levels (safe, low, medium, high) with thresholds Off, Low, Medium or High, and content at the Safe level is always annotated but never blocked.
The Foundry personal data filter scans model output only and can flag or block output.
Llama Guard 4 is a 12B natively multimodal model that runs on one GPU and is a drop-in for Llama Guard 3 8B and 11B, and category text can be rewritten in the prompt.
Guardrails AI runs Input and Output Guards built from Guardrails Hub validators, and the Hub listed 65 validators on 2026-10-13.
Presidio's documentation warns there is no guarantee it finds all PII, and the project moved to the community-owned Data Privacy Stack.
Azure AI Language PII has text PII (synchronous), conversation PII (asynchronous) and document-based PII (asynchronous, native .pdf, .docx and .txt files).
NeMo Guardrails ships built-in content safety, jailbreak detection, topic control, PII handling and fact-checking rails, and its docs list releases from v0.22.0 to v0.24.1 plus a Latest build.
Prompt Shields user prompt attack subtypes include changing system rules, conversation mockup, role-play and encoding attacks.
